passage: Friction is a force that resists the relative motion between two surfaces in contact. It arises due to the interlocking of microscopic irregularities present on all surfaces, even those that appear smooth to the naked eye. Because these tiny bumps exist on every surface, friction is always present, even when an object is at rest. When you try to push a heavy box, static friction acts against your force to keep it stationary. As motion begins, sliding friction takes over. Friction is not just a nuisance; it is essential for our daily activities. For instance, the treads on tires are designed to provide a better grip by increasing the surface area in contact with the road, rather than just locking into bumps. Furthermore, friction is a constant source of energy transformation. Whenever surfaces rub, even at slow speeds, some kinetic energy is converted into heat. This is why machines require lubricants. Lubricants do not melt surfaces; instead, they form a thin layer that separates the two solid surfaces, reducing the interlocking of irregularities. Finally, objects moving through fluids like air or water experience drag. Engineers use streamlining—a specific shape designed to minimize fluid resistance—to help vehicles move efficiently, not merely for aesthetic appeal.

items.evidence: When you try to push a heavy box, static friction acts against your force to keep it stationary.
items.q: You push a heavy box but it stays still. What is friction doing?
options: It pushes back against your force
It is zero until the box starts sliding
It pushes the box along with you
It vanishes because the floor looks smooth
items.explain: Static friction acts against your push and keeps the box stationary, even before it moves.

wrong.why: thinks friction acts only on moving objects
mixes up the direction of the friction force
thinks smooth surfaces have no friction

items.evidence: For instance, the treads on tires are designed to provide a better grip by increasing the surface area in contact with the road, rather than just locking into bumps.
items.q: Why do the treads on a tyre help it grip the road?
options: They put more tyre surface in touch with road
They catch on the bumps in the road
They cut the tyre's contact with the road
They make the road surface smoother
items.explain: Treads give better grip by increasing the surface area touching the road, not just by locking into bumps.

wrong.why: thinks treads only catch on bumps
reverses the effect of treads on contact area
guesses treads change the road, not the tyre

items.evidence: Whenever surfaces rub, even at slow speeds, some kinetic energy is converted into heat.
items.q: You rub your palms together slowly. What happens to the energy of motion?
options: Some of it turns into heat
None turns to heat unless you rub fast
Skin is smooth, so nothing warms up
It is stored inside the palms as force
items.explain: Whenever surfaces rub, even slowly, some kinetic energy is converted into heat.

wrong.why: thinks heat needs very fast rubbing
thinks smooth surfaces give no friction or heat
thinks energy is stored rather than converted

items.evidence: Lubricants do not melt surfaces; instead, they form a thin layer that separates the two solid surfaces, reducing the interlocking of irregularities.
items.q: How does oil help the moving parts of a machine rub less?
options: It keeps a thin layer between the surfaces
It melts the surfaces into a liquid
It polishes all the bumps away completely
It makes the parts lighter to move
items.explain: Lubricants do not melt surfaces; a thin layer separates them and reduces interlocking of bumps.

wrong.why: thinks lubricants turn the surface into a liquid
thinks oil removes the surface bumps entirely
guesses oil changes the weight of the parts

items.evidence: Engineers use streamlining—a specific shape designed to minimize fluid resistance—to help vehicles move efficiently, not merely for aesthetic appeal.
items.q: Why do engineers give fast trains a smooth, pointed front shape?
options: It reduces the air's resistance to motion
It makes them look modern and attractive
It increases drag so they brake better
It removes all friction from the rails
items.explain: Streamlining minimizes fluid resistance so vehicles move efficiently; it is not only for looks.

wrong.why: thinks streamlining is only for looks
reverses the effect of shape on drag
thinks rolling wheels have no friction at all
